title: Flat standard cotangent models for ring sheaves and strict functoriality
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(\mathcal B/\mathcal A)$ be the sheaf standard polynomial resolution and put $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}\mathcal B)$, with $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$, alternating-face differential and zero positive terms, as in [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison]. For every $t\in T$ and $n\geq0$, the stalk $K^{-n}_t$ is the free $\mathcal B_t$-module on the polynomial variables of $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)$. Every term of $K$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $K$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus for every ring-sheaf map $\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$ represents $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$.
For a commutative square $(\mathcal A\to\mathcal B)\to(\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B')$, the standard map sends coefficients by $\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and a free generator $[b]$ to $[b']$ in degree zero, and iterates this rule at each higher polynomial level. It commutes with all faces, degeneracies and augmentations, and induces $\mathrm dp\otimes r\mapsto\mathrm d(p')\otimes r'$ on $K$. These chain maps preserve identities and composition strictly. After tensoring coefficients, they represent the canonical derived functoriality arrows. They commute with open restriction and with the inverse-image comparisons of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison]. For consecutive maps $\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal A$, the maps from $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal D$ to $K_{\mathcal D/\mathcal A}$ agree with their composites through $K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal C}\mathcal D$, using $(v\otimes c)\otimes d\mapsto v\otimes cd$; the same compatibility holds after continuous inverse image.

source.place: Tags 08SR (definition-standard-resolution-sheaves-rings), 08SS (definition-cotangent-complex-morphism-sheaves-rings and subsequent commutative-square maps), 08SV (lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi), 08T4 (lemma-triangle-ringed-spaces, flatness observation); K-flatness from sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat).

proof.text: Form the standard polynomial resolution sectionwise on the open-set site. By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] it has evaluation faces, unit degeneracies and augmentation. By [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], sheafifying its differential complex gives exactly the sheaf complex in the statement. Thus its term in degree $-n$ is $\Omega^1_{P_n/\mathcal A}\otimes_{P_n}\mathcal B$, its differential is the alternating sum of the faces, and its positive terms vanish. The simplicial identities make consecutive alternating sums zero: the terms with indices $i<j$ cancel against the terms obtained using $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$. The image of this actual complex in $D(\mathcal B)$ is $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ by the displayed definition in the affine-comparison statement.

Fix $t\in T$. Let $i_t:\{t\}\to T$ be the continuous inclusion. Inverse image along $i_t$ is the stalk functor, so apply [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] to this map and to its displayed standard construction. The following degreewise calculation specifies the comparison on actual complexes, without inferring a termwise isomorphism from an isomorphism in a derived category. More explicitly, the stalk of a free sheaf algebra $\mathcal R[\mathcal E]$ is $\mathcal R_t[\mathcal E_t]$: a polynomial uses finitely many coefficients and variable labels, so they have representatives on one common neighbourhood; equality of two such polynomials is witnessed after shrinking once for their finitely many coefficients and label identifications. Iterate this argument to identify $(P_n)_t$ with $P_n^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)$, including its labelled variables. The comparison for differentials in [lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials] sends $(\mathrm dp)_t$ to $\mathrm d(p_t)$, and [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] gives
$$(K^{-n})_t\cong\Omega^1_{P_n^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)/\mathcal A_t}\otimes_{P_n^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)}\mathcal B_t.$$
All these are isomorphisms of modules in the specified degree, with the stated ring actions.

source.place: Tags 08SV (lemma-pullback-cotangent-morphism-topoi), 08T0 (lemma-stalk-cotangent-complex); sites-modules.tex Tag 08TQ and modules.tex Tag 01CB

proof.text: Write $P_n^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)=\mathcal A_t[x_e\mid e\in E_{n,t}]$, where $E_{0,t}$ is the underlying set of $\mathcal B_t$ and $E_{n,t}$ for $n>0$ is the underlying set of $P_{n-1}^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] with $R=\mathcal A_t$, $P=P_n^{\mathrm{std}}$ and $S=\mathcal B_t$ via the augmentation. Its scalar-extension clause is written with the coefficient factor first. The swap $\omega\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes\omega$ and its reverse respect the balancing relations since $P$ is commutative. Under this swap $\mathrm dx_e\otimes1$ corresponds to $1\otimes\mathrm dx_e$. Thus that clause identifies the module of step 2 with $\bigoplus_{e\in E_{n,t}}\mathcal B_t\,\mathrm dx_e$. This proves exactly the asserted stalk basis in every nonpositive degree, without any finiteness assumption on the variable set.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differential basis and extension of coefficients

proof.text: Each stalk module just obtained is flat: tensoring any module $M$ by $\bigoplus_{E_{n,t}}\mathcal B_t$ gives the finitely supported families $\bigoplus_{E_{n,t}}M$. A sequence of these families is exact whenever the original sequence is exact, since kernels are coordinatewise and an element with finite support can be lifted one coordinate at a time with the same finite support. For a short exact sequence of $\mathcal B$-module sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] makes its stalk sequence exact; [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] identifies the stalks after tensoring with $K^{-n}$ with the tensor of that sequence by the free stalk module. The resulting sheaf sequence is exact by the converse stalk criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. Therefore tensoring by $K^{-n}$ is exact, which is flatness by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The positive zero terms have the same property.

source.place: Tag 05NE (lemma-flat-stalks-flat), forward proof from flat stalks, with the free-module coordinate argument written out

proof.text: The complex $K$ is bounded above by $0$, and step 4 proves that all its terms are flat. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to the open-set site of $T$ and its ring sheaf $\mathcal B$. Its hypotheses are exactly these two properties, so $K$ is K-flat. No lower bound on $K$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); the existing node cites this lemma with a stale numerical tag 06YS

proof.text: For any ring-sheaf map $\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, apply clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the same open-set site. Use the identity quasi-isomorphism $K\to K$ as the K-flat resolution, justified by step 5. Write $Q_{\mathcal C}$ for passage from complexes to $D(\mathcal C)$. The node gives the canonical comparison isomorphism $\theta_K:L\varphi^*Q_{\mathcal B}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal C}(K\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C)$, with the direction prescribed in its clause (2). Step 1 identifies $Q_{\mathcal B}(K)$ with $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$, so this is exactly the required derived scalar-extension representation. No flatness of $\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal B$ is assumed. The representative also has flat terms by step 4, meeting the flat-term hypothesis of Stacks 06YY as well as the K-flat hypothesis of the cited node.

Let $(\alpha,\beta):(\mathcal A\to\mathcal B)\to(\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B')$ be the given square. On sectionwise standard resolutions put $t_{-1}=\beta$ and define $t_0$ by $a\mapsto\alpha(a)$, $[b]\mapsto[\beta(b)]$; recursively $t_n:\mathcal A[UP_{n-1}]\to\mathcal A'[UP'_{n-1}]$ sends $[p]\mapsto[t_{n-1}(p)]$. The ring-square maps of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] give exactly these maps, commuting with all faces, degeneracies and augmentations. They commute with restriction because restriction is another square of rings and those ring-square maps compose strictly. Sheafify using the sectionwise construction of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison]. This produces the asserted maps on sheaf resolutions. For an identity square the recursion fixes coefficients and variables. For two squares the recursive composite sends $[p]$ to $[t'_{n-1}t_{n-1}(p)]$, which is the direct recursion for the composite square. Uniqueness of polynomial maps with specified coefficients and generator values proves strict equality before and after sheafification.

source.place: Tag 08SS, commutative-square construction immediately after definition-cotangent-complex-morphism-sheaves-rings; Tag 08QL (section-functoriality)

proof.text: In degree $-n$ send $\mathrm dp\otimes r$ to $\mathrm d(t_n p)\otimes\beta(r)$. This is well defined by the presentation of differentials in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: additivity and Leibniz relations map to those same relations in the target, and the differential of a source coefficient maps to the differential of its image in $\mathcal A'$, which is zero. The balancing relation $q\,\mathrm dp\otimes r=\mathrm dp\otimes\epsilon(q)r$ is respected since $\epsilon't_n=\beta\epsilon$. Commutation with each face in step 7 gives commutation with the alternating differential. For two squares, both composite maps send a generating expression $\mathrm dp\otimes r$ to $\mathrm d(t'_nt_np)\otimes\beta'\beta(r)$; for the identity square this is $\mathrm dp\otimes r$. Hence the induced semilinear chain maps preserve identities and composition strictly.

source.place: Tag 08SS, maps on differentials following equation-commutative-square-sheaves; algebra.tex Tag 07BK (definition-differentials)

proof.text: Linearize the semilinear chain map of step 8 to a $\mathcal B\prime$-linear map $f:K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B\prime\to K_{\mathcal B\prime/\mathcal A\prime}$, sending $(\mathrm dp\otimes r)\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(t_n p)\otimes\beta(r)c$. Set $\mathcal C=\mathcal B\prime$ in step 6. The represented derived arrow is precisely $Q_{\mathcal B\prime}(f)\circ\theta_K$, with source $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B\prime$ and target $L_{\mathcal B\prime/\mathcal A\prime}$. The canonical cotangent functoriality arrow is defined by this same map of standard differential models: this is the sheaf construction in [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], and sectionwise it is the standard square map of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] supplies exactly the canonical $\theta_K$, so the displayed composite represents that arrow with its prescribed comparison, not just an abstractly isomorphic source. The coefficient in its pure-tensor formula lies in $\mathcal B\prime$ throughout.

source.place: Tag 08SS, functoriality after the definition; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YT and 06YY, computation on K-flat models

proof.text: The inverse-image and open-restriction comparisons of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] are natural in the sheaf-ring map. Their normalization on differentials is fixed by [lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials]: the inverse image of $\mathrm dp$ goes to the differential of the inverse image of $p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] with $R=P_n$, $S=u^{-1}P_n$, $c=\mathrm{id}$, $M=\Omega^1_{P_n/\mathcal A}$ and $N=\mathcal B$ (the last a $P_n$-module via augmentation). It identifies $u^{-1}(M\otimes_{P_n}\mathcal B)$ with $u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}P_n}u^{-1}\mathcal B$ by the pure-tensor formula. The differential comparison identifies the first factor over $u^{-1}P_n$. On a free-algebra generator, the polynomial comparison sends the inverse image of $[p]$ to the variable labelled by the inverse image of $p$: this is its defining free-algebra universal property. Consequently both orders of applying inverse image and step 7 send each variable $[p]$ to $[u^{-1}(t_np)]$, and both orders for step 8 send $u^{-1}(\mathrm dp\otimes r)$ to $\mathrm d(u^{-1}(t_np))\otimes u^{-1}(\beta(r))$. Polynomial maps are determined by variables and coefficients, while differential tensor modules are generated locally by these expressions; hence the comparison squares commute as chain maps. Taking an open inclusion proves the open-restriction assertion as well.

For $\mathcal B\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal C\xrightarrow{k}\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal A$, write $h:K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\to K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}$ and $g:K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\to K_{\mathcal D/\mathcal A}$ for the semilinear maps. Step 8 says the direct map is $gh$. The reassociation $((v\otimes c)\otimes d)\mapsto v\otimes k(c)d$ has inverse $v\otimes d\mapsto(v\otimes1)\otimes d$; both formulas respect balancing, and their composites are identities by the balancing relation. On $v=\mathrm dp\otimes r$, the route through $K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal C}\mathcal D$ sends $((v\otimes c)\otimes d)$ to $gh(v)\,k(c)d$. The direct route sends its reassociated tensor to that same expression. This proves the required equality on generators and hence on the complexes. Applying the comparisons of step 10 gives precisely the same formula with $u^{-1}j,u^{-1}k$ and inverse-image sections, so the equality also holds after every continuous inverse image. Step 9 identifies these equalities with the canonical derived arrows.
